subject.title: fix(runtime): cancelled workflows no longer continue external commands

question: Should Lobster permanently treat a workflow resume as consumed once its first step-dispatch boundary is crossed and a later parent cancellation occurs, while preserving the same resume for cancellations during async setup?
rationale: This is a user-visible reliability and replay-safety contract for persisted workflow capabilities; the patch implements a coherent boundary, but source evidence alone cannot choose the product semantics of retry versus one-time consumption after partially started execution.

options.title: Confirm one-time post-start resumes
options.body: Merge with the proposed boundary: setup-time cancellation remains retryable, while cancellation after dispatch begins removes the resume capability to prevent replay of side effects.

options.title: Preserve retries after cancellation
options.body: Keep resume state after post-start cancellation, accepting that workflows with completed side effects need a different idempotency or replay model.

recommendation.title: Confirm one-time post-start resumes
recommendation.body: Merge with the proposed boundary: setup-time cancellation remains retryable, while cancellation after dispatch begins removes the resume capability to prevent replay of side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this contributor directly to the precise cancellation and resume-state boundary under review; no independent current-main owner was available in the provided evidence.
